newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal government narrowly survives confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Nepal government narrowly survives confidence vote.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's 15-month-old coalition on Tuesday narrowly survived a parliamentary no-confidence vote, parliament officials said.
The main opposition Unified Marxist Leninist (UML) party failed by two votes to muster the necessary majority to win the no-confidence motion.
The officials said the House of Representatives, the lower house of parliament, rejected a no-confidence motion moved by the UML party by 101 votes to 84.
Nepal's constitution requires that a no-confidence motion attract at least 103 votes to gain a majority in the 205-member house.

The no-confidence vote was precipitated by a split within one of the junior partners in Deuba's three-party coalition. It is the second time in less than a year that Deuba has survived a no-confidence motion.
